doc.name: A — bed linen catalogue, chrome podium, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: stonewashed linen duvet set
Category: bed linen
Shot programme: chrome podium
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You are the still-life director on a commercial bed linen shoot. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the macro detail insert in a chrome podium treatment.

SUBJECT. A stonewashed linen duvet set. Product fidelity is non-negotiable: shape, seams, cap, closure, print placement and colour must match the reference precisely. Only the scene around it is yours to author.

CAMERA. Extreme macro on the closure, seam, texture or applicator — product only partly in frame. Shoot on an 85mm short telephoto at f/22, framing for a stacked layered composition with three depth planes.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with bare-bulb specular light producing tight, hot speculars. Stage the product on or against hand-thrown ceramic, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a clean high-key grade with the whites pushed to the edge of clipping. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Return ONE image-generation prompt as a single unbroken paragraph. No preamble, no headings, no bullet points, no commentary, no markdown.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.
